subject: Request: Nightly shim & versioning SLA for partner SDK (AgentBridge)
messages:
From: Kara Simmons <kara@agentbridge.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AgentBridge request: nightly shim for upcoming API v3 removal

Hi Aditya,

Hope you’re well — quick note from the AgentBridge product team. We recently finished running our integration tests against Redwood’s public API and discovered that the upcoming api-v3 removal will break our SDK paths and a set of enterprise customers who embed our agent routing layer.

We have two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a nightly compatibility "shim" or backwards-wrapper for api-v3 behavior for the deprecation window? We’d like nightly builds we can run in CI while we migrate.
- Can we get a formal versioning SLA / deprecation guarantee (minimum window, rollback options, and a small-number-of-requests emergency rollback path) so we can commit to timelines with our customers?

Attached is a short proposal that sketches our compatibility concerns and a suggested shim (agentbridge-shim-proposal.pdf). We’d prefer not to hold up your roadmap, but we also need a pragmatic migration plan that protects customers.

Can you confirm whether this is feasible and what a rough timeline looks like? Also looping in my engineering lead Nikhil (cc) who can jump into a technical call.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

— Kara
Kara Simmons
Head of Platform Partnerships | AgentBridge
kara@agentbridge.io
+1 415-555-0172

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kara Simmons <kara@agentbridge.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AgentBridge request: nightly shim for upcoming API v3 removal

Kara — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. We want to avoid breaking partner integrations and keep migrations predictable, so this is the right kind of conversation.

High-level response / proposal:
- Short term (CI-nightly): Redwood can publish a nightly "v3-compat" shim image that implements the subset of behaviors AgentBridge calls today. This would be an opt-in artifact intended for partner CI and smoke tests.
- Medium term (deprecation SLA): we propose a 9-month deprecation window from public announcement for api-v3, with a documented rollback path (feature flag + image tag we can flip) and prioritized hotfixes for enterprise customers on Dedicated.
- Commercial/ops: for customers who need guaranteed backports or an SLA above the 9 months, we can offer a paid support add-on (reserved-eng hours) to accelerate fixes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas — can you estimate engineering effort for a minimal shim (prototype) and full compatibility build + test harness? Please call out what we cannot safely emulate (e.g., deprecated runtime kernels, older quantization formats).
2) Marissa / Vanessa — I’ll need partner comms and legal to draft an SLA and sample mutual action plan (MAP).
3) Kara / Nikhil — if you can share a prioritized call graph or top-10 API endpoints you rely on, that will speed triage.

I’ve attached an initial compatibility matrix (compat-matrix-v3-v2.xlsx) I asked the team to populate with what we know; it’s terse but should help.

I’ll block time for a sync once Jonas responds with estimates. Thanks — good to solve this proactively.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kara Simmons <kara@agentbridge.io>, Nikhil Rao <nikhil@agentbridge.io>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AgentBridge request: nightly shim for upcoming API v3 removal

Aditya / team / Kara — quick technical readout. I dug into the shim proposal and sketched the following:

What a minimal v3-compat shim looks like (prototype):
- A thin HTTP adapter layer that translates v3 request shapes to api-v4 internal calls and maps error shapes back to v3. No model logic changes.
- A compatibility test harness with the top-10 API flows (as Aditya requested) and nightly run in CI against the shim image.

Engineering estimates (rough):
- Prototype shim + CI smoke tests: 4–6 weeks (one engineer + part-time infra support). Prototype covers most request/response translations but not exhaustive format edge cases.
- Full compatibility build (edge cases, quantization fallback tests, extensive regression suite, docs): 12–14 weeks. Full test-suite required before we mark nightly artifacts as "recommended for customer CI."

Technical risks / caveats:
- Quantization/formats: we cannot fully emulate some older quantized kernel paths on newer runtimes without larger runtime changes. Those will need to be surfaced explicitly in the compat matrix and treated as "unsupported but mitigable" items.
- Performance delta: shim adds translation overhead; for latency-sensitive customers we should clearly label nightly artifacts as test-only unless they accept a performance SLA change.
- Build & signing: nightly artifacts will need a separate CI pipeline & signing process; ops will need to grant AgentBridge account access to nightly read-only artifacts.

Suggested rollout plan:
- Week 0–6: prototype shim + internal verification; share nightly artifact with AgentBridge (read-only).
- Week 7–14: expand tests, add regression suite, document limitations, publish compatibility matrix & MAP.
- Post-week 14: formal deprecation announcement + 9-month coexisting window.

Action items (mine): I’ll start a small spike tomorrow and post the first prototype by Week 3. I recommend we document all exceptions up-front and include them in the MAP.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime Compatibility | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwoodinference.com

From: Kara Simmons <kara@agentbridge.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Rao <nikhil@agentbridge.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AgentBridge request: nightly shim for upcoming API v3 removal

Thanks — that readout is really helpful. We’re aligned on the high-level approach and appreciate the realistic risk callouts.

Quick confirmations / asks:
- AgentBridge is happy to accept nightly artifacts as "CI-only" while we migrate; please provide read-only access to the artifact storage and a weekly changelog for the first 6 weeks.
- The proposed 9-month deprecation window sounds acceptable to our enterprise customers, as long as there is a documented emergency rollback process (feature flag + image tag) and a committed contact for hotfix triage.
- Can Redwood share SOC-related artifacts (SOC 2 summary, audit contact) in parallel for our procurement team? If possible, add them to the MAP doc.

I’ll route the MAP + prioritized endpoint list later today. Also: prior to the plan going public with our customers we’ll want a short canary plan (small cohort, 2-week monitoring, rollback thresholds). Would Redwood be able to support that as part of the rollout?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’ll get our MAP over and would like to schedule a 30-minute sync next Tue (your availability?).
